questions.q: For a reinforced concrete beam with a clear span of 4.0 meters, what is the minimum recommended camber to be provided according to the L/360 deflection limit?
questions.n: L/360 for a 4000mm span is 11.11mm. In practical site application, this is rounded up to the nearest workable increment, which is 12 mm.

questions.q: What is the minimum concrete cover (mm) required for reinforcing steel in concrete cast against and permanently exposed to earth (e.g., footings without forms)?
questions.n: Per NSCP/ACI, concrete cast directly against the earth without forms requires a minimum cover of 75mm to protect against moisture and soil chemicals.

questions.q: In the NSCP, what is the specified maximum slump (mm) allowed for concrete used in beams and reinforced slabs to ensure proper flow without compromising strength?
questions.n: For reinforced beams and slabs, 100 mm (4 inches) is the standard maximum slump to maintain the structural integrity of the mix.

questions.q: According to the provided strength classification, what is the minimum compressive strength for a Class A concrete mixture?
questions.n: Based on the updated scale provided, Class A is specified at 3500 psi.

questions.q: When specifying structural steel, which part of a Wide Flange (W) section is designed to resist the majority of the bending moment?
questions.n: The top and bottom flanges provide the most resistance to bending moments by handling the compressive and tensile stresses.

questions.q: What is the minimum concrete cover (mm) for a reinforced concrete beam that is not exposed to weather or in contact with the ground, according to the NSCP?
questions.n: The NSCP specifies 40 mm as the standard concrete cover for beams and columns to protect the primary reinforcement from corrosion and fire.

questions.q: Which type of cement is specifically designed to resist sulfate attack, making it suitable for structures in contact with seawater?
questions.n: Type V Portland cement is specifically manufactured for high resistance to sulfate attack, critical for marine environments.

questions.q: What is the purpose of providing 'camber' in the formwork of a long-span horizontal structural member?
o: To reduce the amount of concrete needed
To improve the tensile strength of steel
questions.n: Cambering provides an initial upward curvature so that the member appears level after it settles under its own weight and dead loads.

questions.q: In a steel Wide Flange (W) beam, which part of the cross-section is primarily responsible for resisting vertical shear forces?
questions.n: The vertical portion (web) of the beam provides the cross-sectional area required to resist shear stresses.

questions.q: What is the standard weight of one bag of Portland cement in the Philippines?
questions.n: 40 kg is the standard unit weight for a single bag of cement in the local market for volumetric mixing.

questions.q: According to the NSCP, what is the maximum spacing of lateral ties for a tied column based on the diameter of the longitudinal bars?
questions.n: The code specifies that tie spacing shall not exceed 16 times the diameter of the longitudinal reinforcing bars.

questions.q: Which property of concrete describes its ability to resist being squeezed or crushed?
questions.n: Compressive strength is the primary structural characteristic of concrete, measured in PSI or MPa.

questions.q: For a 'Class B' concrete mix, what is the typical ratio of Cement:Sand:Gravel by volume?
questions.n: Class B concrete, used for slabs on fill or minor structural elements, follows the 1:2.5:5 ratio.

questions.q: What is the primary disadvantage of using high-strength concrete in a standard architectural project?
o: It allows for smaller column sizes
It is more susceptible to brittle failure
It is easier to pump to high altitudes
It dries slower than normal concrete
questions.n: High-strength concrete lacks the ductility of lower-strength mixes and can fail suddenly without warning if not reinforced properly.

questions.q: In structural steel design, what is 'galvanizing'?
o: The process of heating steel to increase hardness
The chemical cleaning of steel before painting
The application of a zinc coating to prevent corrosion
The welding of two different types of metal
questions.n: Galvanizing creates a sacrificial layer of zinc that protects the underlying steel from rust through electrochemical action.

questions.q: What is the minimum curing time (days) for standard concrete before it reaches its 70% design strength?
questions.n: Concrete typically achieves about 65% to 70% of its 28-day design strength within the first week of proper curing.

questions.q: Which structural member is used to transfer the loads from a building's columns or walls directly to the soil?
questions.n: The footing spreads the concentrated load of the column over a wider area of soil to prevent sinking.

questions.q: In a reinforced concrete slab, where are the 'temperature bars' primarily placed?
o: Only at the edges of the slab
At the bottom of the footing
questions.n: Temperature and shrinkage bars are placed in the secondary direction to control cracks caused by thermal expansion.

questions.q: What is the result of adding too much water to a concrete mix (increasing the water-cement ratio)?
questions.n: The water-to-cement ratio is inversely proportional to strength; more water equals weaker concrete.

questions.q: Which foundation type is most suitable for a site with very steep slopes where you want to avoid massive excavation?
questions.n: Stepped footings allow the foundation to 'follow' the natural grade of the hill, minimizing earthwork.

questions.q: In the Philippines, what is the nominal diameter (mm) of a #4 reinforcing steel bar?
questions.n: A #4 bar is equivalent to a 12.7 mm bar, commonly referred to and sold as 12 mm in local practice.

questions.q: What is the effect of 'segregation' in a concrete mix during pouring?
o: Coarse aggregates settle at the bottom
questions.n: Segregation occurs when the heavy stones separate from the mortar, often due to dropping concrete from too high a height.

questions.q: Which structural component provides a level surface for roof shingles or metal sheets and transfers the load to the rafters?
questions.n: Purlins are horizontal beams that span between trusses or rafters to support the roof cladding.

questions.q: What is 'creep' in structural concrete?
o: The expansion of concrete due to heat
The slow deformation under a constant load over time
The movement of water through pores
questions.n: Concrete will continue to deflect or deform slightly over years if it is under a permanent compressive load.

questions.q: In the Philippines, which metal is typically used for 'tie wires' to secure reinforcing bars together?
questions.n: Annealed black iron wire or G.I. wire (Gauge 16) is the industry standard for tying rebars.

questions.q: When a soil boring test is conducted for a standard low-rise building in the Philippines, what is the generally accepted minimum depth (meters) the boring must reach?
questions.n: Standard soil exploration for light structures typically starts at a minimum depth of 1.5 meters to find stable bearing strata.

questions.q: Which specific type of footing is designed to support two or more columns in a row, often used when columns are so close that individual footings would overlap?
questions.n: A combined footing is a single structural element that supports two or more column loads, distributing them to the soil.

questions.q: What is the result of 'honeycombing' in a reinforced concrete beam after the forms are stripped?
o: Exposure of reinforcement and reduced structural integrity
questions.n: Honeycombs are voids where mortar failed to fill the spaces between coarse aggregates, leaving rebars vulnerable to rust.

questions.q: In structural steel, what is the function of a 'gusset plate'?
o: To increase the weight of the column
To provide fireproofing to the beam
To act as a decorative trim
To connect multiple structural members at a joint
questions.n: Gusset plates are thick sheets of steel used to join chords, trusses, or beams at a single intersection point.

questions.q: According to the NSCP, what is the minimum thickness (mm) for a concrete footing supporting a permanent building structure?
questions.n: The code requires at least 250 mm of thickness to ensure proper load distribution and protection of reinforcement.

questions.q: What is the primary structural purpose of a 'shear wall' in a high-rise building?
o: To support the weight of the roof
To resist lateral forces such as wind and earthquakes
To house the plumbing and electrical risers
To provide sound insulation between units
questions.n: Shear walls are stiff vertical diaphragms that prevent the building from swaying or collapsing under horizontal loads.

questions.q: In a wood-framed structure, which horizontal member is placed directly on top of the foundation to provide a flat surface for the rest of the frame?
questions.n: The sill plate is the lowest wooden member of the frame, anchored directly to the concrete foundation.

questions.q: What happens to the 'slump' of concrete if the temperature of the mix increases significantly during transportation?
questions.n: Heat causes faster evaporation and chemical reaction, leading to a loss of workability and a lower slump.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a standard component of a typical roof truss?
questions.n: Stirrups are U-shaped reinforcing bars used in concrete beams to resist shear, not truss components.

questions.q: When stripping forms for a concrete beam, which part of the formwork should be removed LAST for safety and structural stability?
questions.n: The soffit supports the entire weight of the beam and must remain until the concrete has reached sufficient strength.

questions.q: What is the primary reason for vibrating concrete immediately after it is poured into the forms?
o: To make the concrete surface smoother
To remove trapped air and consolidate the mix
To speed up the drying time
questions.n: Vibration ensures that the concrete settles into all corners and eliminates air pockets that would weaken the structure.

questions.q: For a standard residential building, what is the typical live load (kg/sqm) used for the design of the ground floor, according to the NSCP?
questions.n: 200 kg/sqm (approx. 1.9 kPa) is the standard residential live load for floors.

questions.q: In structural metallurgy, 'galvanic corrosion' is most likely to occur when:
o: Aluminum is used in a very dry climate
Steel is left unpainted in the sun
Two dissimilar metals are in contact in a moist environment
questions.n: Galvanic corrosion happens when metals with different electrical potentials (like copper and steel) touch in the presence of an electrolyte.

questions.q: What is the minimum concrete cover (mm) for reinforcement in a concrete wall exposed to weather, when using #6 bars or larger?
questions.n: The NSCP specifies 50 mm (2 inches) of cover for larger bars (#6 to #18) in weather-exposed walls.

questions.q: Which material is often added to concrete as an 'admixture' to slow down the setting time, useful in hot tropical climates?
questions.n: Retarders delay the chemical reaction of hydration, allowing more time for pouring and finishing in hot weather.

questions.q: In a steel 'Box Beam,' what is the primary structural advantage compared to a standard I-beam?
o: It is lighter for the same depth
It has much higher torsional (twisting) resistance
It is easier to bolt to other members
questions.n: The closed-loop shape of a box beam makes it significantly better at resisting twisting forces than an open I-shape.

questions.q: According to the NSCP, foundations should NOT rest on which type of material?
questions.n: Foundations must rest on natural, undisturbed soil or engineered, compacted fill; uncompacted fill leads to unpredictable sinking.

questions.q: What is 'Modulus of Elasticity' (E) a measure of in structural materials?
o: The weight of the material per volume
questions.n: The modulus of elasticity describes how much a material will deflect or stretch under a given load while still returning to its original shape.

questions.q: Which type of stress is a 'diagonal tension' crack in a concrete beam an indicator of?
questions.n: Diagonal tension is the result of vertical and horizontal shear forces combining, leading to 45-degree cracks.

questions.q: For a concrete slab on grade, why are 'control joints' used?
o: To pre-determine where shrinkage cracks will occur
To make the slab thicker at the edges
To allow the slab to expand in the sun
To separate the slab from the building columns
questions.n: By creating a 'weakened plane' in the slab, you ensure that natural drying cracks happen in a straight line inside the joint.

questions.q: In a standard 4-meter clear span concrete beam, the minimum camber of 6 mm (per local rule of thumb) represents what percentage of the total span length?
questions.n: Calculation: (6 / 4000) * 100 = 0.15%. This matches the 1.5mm/meter simplified rule.

questions.q: What is the primary function of 'base plates' at the bottom of a steel column?
o: To allow the column to rotate during an earthquake
To increase the height of the column
To prevent the steel from rusting
To distribute the concentrated column load to the concrete foundation
questions.n: Concrete is much weaker than steel in compression, so a wide base plate spreads the load to avoid crushing the concrete pedestal.

questions.q: Which aggregate size is most commonly specified for standard reinforced concrete slabs that are 100mm to 150mm thick?
questions.n: 3/4" G-1 gravel is the standard 'coarse aggregate' size that balances strength, workability, and cost.

questions.q: What is 'Pre-stressed Concrete'?
o: Concrete that has been cured for more than 28 days
Concrete that is vibrated before it is poured
Concrete that contains no steel reinforcement
Concrete with internal steel tendons that are tensioned to compress the concrete
questions.n: By putting the concrete in permanent compression, it can resist much higher loads without cracking in tension.

questions.q: In the Philippines, what is the standard length (meters) of a commercial reinforcing steel bar?
questions.n: 6 meters (approx. 20 feet) is the standard stock length for rebars in the local market.

questions.q: What is 'bleeding' in a concrete mixture?
o: When the cement leaks through gaps in the formwork
When the concrete turns red due to rust
When the concrete cracks immediately after pouring
When water rises to the surface of freshly placed concrete
questions.n: As heavier particles settle, excess water is pushed to the top, which can weaken the surface if it's too excessive.

questions.q: Which structural steel shape is typically preferred for columns because its width and depth are nearly equal?
questions.n: W-shapes with 'square' proportions (e.g., W10x49) have high stiffness in both axes, ideal for resisting column buckling.

questions.q: In foundation design, what is 'Differential Settlement'?
o: When the soil expands due to moisture
When the building floats on top of the soil
When the entire building sinks at the same rate
When one part of the building sinks more than another part
questions.n: Uneven sinking causes severe structural cracking and can lead to the total failure of the frame.

questions.q: What is the function of 'stirrups' in a reinforced concrete beam?
o: To hold the top and bottom bars apart
To increase the compressive strength of the concrete
questions.n: Stirrups are placed vertically to cross potential 45-degree shear cracks and 'stitch' them back together.

questions.q: Which of the following is a 'dead load' in a building?
o: Weight of the concrete slab itself
questions.n: Dead loads are the permanent, immovable weights of the structure's own components.

questions.q: According to the NSCP, what is the 'yield strength' (Fy) of standard Grade 40 reinforcing steel commonly used in the Philippines?
questions.n: Grade 40 steel has a yield strength of 275 MPa, the standard for residential construction.

questions.q: What is the purpose of 'lap splicing' reinforcing bars?
o: To make the bars easier to bend
To transfer the load from one bar to another when a single length is not enough
questions.n: By overlapping bars by a specific length, the tension or compression is passed through the concrete from one bar to the next.

questions.q: In site planning, what does 'Topography' refer to?
o: The physical features and elevations of the land surface
The type of trees on the site
The chemical composition of the soil
The legal boundaries of the property
questions.n: Topography describes the 'lay of the land,' including slopes, hills, and valleys.

questions.q: Which structural system uses a series of triangles to span large distances with minimal material?
questions.n: The triangle is the only geometric shape that cannot be deformed without changing the length of its sides, making trusses extremely efficient.

questions.q: What is 'Curing' of concrete?
o: Maintaining moisture and temperature to ensure proper hydration
The chemical reaction that makes concrete hot
The process of mixing the cement and water
The moment the concrete is poured into the forms
questions.n: Hydration is a long chemical process; curing ensures there is enough water available for the cement to fully react and harden.

questions.q: In the Philippines, what is the most common thickness (mm) of a non-load bearing interior CHB partition?
questions.n: 4-inch (100 mm) CHB is the standard for non-structural interior walls.

questions.q: What is the structural effect of 'over-reinforced' concrete beams?
o: They are lighter and easier to install
They are much safer because they have extra steel
They fail suddenly by concrete crushing without warning
They are more flexible and can sway more
questions.n: If there's too much steel, the concrete will crush before the steel yields, leading to a sudden, brittle, and explosive failure.

questions.q: Which aggregate is used to make 'lightweight concrete'?
questions.n: These volcanic or engineered materials contain air pockets that reduce the overall weight of the concrete mix.

questions.q: In a steel beam-to-column connection, what is a 'moment connection'?
o: A connection that allows the beam to slide
A temporary connection used during construction
A connection that only handles vertical loads
A rigid connection that transfers both shear and bending forces
questions.n: Moment connections prevent any rotation between the beam and column, making the entire frame act as a single unit.

questions.q: What is the main advantage of using 'Fly Ash' as a partial replacement for cement in concrete?
o: It makes the concrete harden in 1 hour
It improves workability and reduces heat of hydration
It makes the concrete turn bright white
It increases the weight of the concrete
questions.n: Fly ash acts as a lubricant (spherical particles) and slows down the heat release, which is great for mass concrete.

questions.q: According to the NSCP, what is the 'minimum depth' (mm) for a concrete beam, unless a more detailed deflection calculation is performed?
questions.n: For a simple span beam, the minimum depth is L/16 to control deflection without extra math.

questions.q: In site construction, what is a 'batter board'?
o: A board used to smooth out wet concrete
A protective board for workers to walk on
A board used to support the sides of a trench
A temporary framework used to mark the building's corners and layout
questions.n: Batter boards hold the strings that define the exact location of walls and foundations during excavation.

questions.q: Which structural member is designed to carry the load of a wall across a door or window opening?
questions.n: A lintel (in masonry) or header (in wood) spans the opening to transfer the weight of the wall above to the side supports.

questions.q: What is the 'Modulus of Rupture' of concrete?
o: The speed at which concrete cracks
The tensile strength of concrete measured in a bending test
The maximum temperature concrete can survive
The strength of concrete in pure tension
questions.n: It represents the ability of an unreinforced concrete beam to resist failure in bending.

questions.q: What is the structural effect of 'honeycombing' in a reinforced concrete beam after the forms are stripped?
o: Exposure of reinforcement and reduced structural integrity
questions.n: Honeycombs are voids where mortar failed to fill the spaces between coarse aggregates, leaving rebars vulnerable to rust.

questions.q: What is the maximum depth of a control joint in a 150mm thick concrete slab on grade to effectively manage shrinkage cracks?
questions.n: A depth of 1/4 the total slab thickness (150mm / 4) provides the necessary structural guidance for crack formation.

questions.q: In structural steel, what is the primary purpose of a 'Girt' in a framed wall system?
o: To provide lateral support to the wall panel
To act as a primary vertical load-bearing member
To support floor loads from the deck
To connect the foundation to the sill plate
questions.n: Girts are horizontal members fastened to columns to resist wind loads and support siding materials.

questions.q: According to the NSCP, what is the minimum concrete cover (mm) for a reinforced concrete wall that is NOT exposed to weather or in contact with ground, using #5 bars or smaller?
questions.n: The NSCP specifies 20mm for walls and slabs not exposed to weather when using smaller bar sizes.

questions.q: Which specific type of cement is characterized by a high rate of strength development, reaching its design strength much faster than Portland Type I?
questions.n: High alumina cement is known for very rapid hardening and high early strength within 24 hours.

questions.q: What is the maximum spacing of vertical stiffener columns in a standard 150mm CHB wall as per common Philippine practice?
questions.n: The code and local standards generally mandate stiffeners at every 3 meters of wall length.

W12×65, what does the number '65' represent?
o: The yield strength of the steel in ksi
The depth of the beam in inches
The weight of the beam in pounds per linear foot
The width of the flange in inches
questions.n: The second number in a W-shape designation indicates the weight per unit length.

questions.q: What is the minimum recommended fire rating for a 150mm (6-inch) thick concrete hollow block wall with a fine aggregate mix?
questions.n: Standard 150mm CHB walls are generally accepted to meet a 2-hour fire-resistance rating.

questions.q: Which structural member is used to provide a level horizontal surface at the base of a wood stud wall, connecting it to the concrete floor?
questions.n: The sole plate is the bottom horizontal member of a wall frame that sits on the floor or sill plate.

questions.q: In the context of the NSCP, what is the 'minimum' thickness of a non-bearing masonry partition wall?
questions.n: 100mm (4 inches) is the standard minimum thickness for interior non-load-bearing masonry walls.

questions.q: What is the result of using 'aggregates' that are too large for a specific reinforced concrete member?
o: Difficulty in passing through reinforcement bars
questions.n: Oversized aggregates can get stuck between rebars, causing voids or honeycombing.

questions.q: When stripping formwork, what is the generally recommended minimum period before removing the sidings of beams and columns?
questions.n: Non-load-bearing vertical forms can be removed as soon as the concrete is hard enough to resist damage.

questions.q: Which type of stress is a 'Stirrup' in a reinforced concrete beam specifically designed to resist?
questions.n: Stirrups provide the necessary reinforcement to counteract shear-induced diagonal cracks.

questions.q: In the Philippines, what is the standard diameter of a #3 reinforcing bar in millimeters?
questions.n: #3 bars are approximately 3/8 of an inch, which is standardized as 10mm in the metric system.

questions.q: What is the primary structural function of 'Temperature Bars' in a one-way slab?
o: To prevent shrinkage and thermal cracking
To carry the primary live loads
To act as a moisture barrier
questions.n: These bars are placed perpendicular to the main bars to control cracks from environmental changes.

questions.q: Which foundation type is best described as a thick, reinforced concrete slab that covers the entire area under a building to support all columns and walls?
questions.n: A mat foundation acts as one large unit to distribute heavy loads across a wide area of soil.

questions.q: According to the NSCP, what is the minimum compressive strength (f'c) for concrete used in footings and slabs on grade?
questions.n: 2500 psi (approx. 17 MPa) is a common minimum for residential slabs and light footings.

questions.q: What is the term for the vertical distance from the top of the foundation to the lowest part of the footing?
questions.n: The depth of footing is the vertical measurement from the grade or floor level to the base of the footing.

questions.q: In structural steel design, why are 'Box Beams' or hollow structural sections (HSS) preferred for members subjected to twisting?
questions.n: The closed shape of a box beam allows it to resist twisting much more effectively than an open I-shape.

questions.q: What is the standard weight of a bag of cement in the Philippines as commonly used in construction estimates?
questions.n: The 40kg bag is the standard unit for Portland cement in the Philippines.

questions.q: Which building material property is specifically improved by 'Curing'?
questions.n: Proper curing ensures hydration of cement, leading to the full development of compressive strength.

questions.q: When casting concrete against earth without forms, such as in a typical footing, what is the minimum concrete cover required for all reinforcement?
questions.n: A larger cover is necessary when concrete is poured directly against the soil to account for surface irregularities and potential moisture penetration.

questions.q: Which type of cement is most appropriate for a structure being built in a coastal area with high exposure to seawater?
questions.n: Seawater contains high concentrations of sulfates, and this cement type is chemically formulated to resist sulfate-induced expansion and decay.

questions.q: In a steel Wide Flange (W) beam, which part of the cross-section is primarily designed to resist bending moments?
questions.n: By placing the majority of the material furthest from the neutral axis, the flanges efficiently handle the tension and compression caused by bending.

questions.q: What is the primary structural function of 'Temperature Bars' in a one-way reinforced concrete slab?
o: To carry the primary dead and live loads
To control cracks caused by shrinkage and thermal expansion
To increase the compressive strength of the concrete
questions.n: These bars are placed perpendicular to the main reinforcement to maintain the slab's integrity against environmental changes.

questions.q: According to common construction practice in the Philippines, what is the maximum recommended height for a CHB wall before a horizontal stiffener beam (lintel/bond beam) is required?
questions.n: At this height, the wall becomes susceptible to lateral instability, requiring a horizontal member to tie the system together.

questions.q: What happens to the workability and ultimate strength of a concrete mix if the water-cement ratio is significantly increased?
questions.n: The extra water makes the concrete easier to pour but leaves more pores after evaporation, reducing the density and strength.

questions.q: In foundation engineering, which type of footing is characterized by a series of 'steps' to accommodate a change in elevation while keeping the footing horizontal?
questions.n: This design allows the foundation to follow a slope in discrete intervals, minimizing deep excavation on one side.

questions.q: Which structural steel shape is best suited to resist torsional (twisting) forces due to its closed cross-section?
questions.n: The closed loop of the section provides a continuous path for shear flow, making it exceptionally rigid against torsion.

) of Grade 60 reinforcing steel commonly used for heavy structural members in the Philippines?
questions.n: Grade 60 steel, with a yield strength of 414 MPa (60,000 psi), is the standard for high-strength structural reinforcement.

questions.q: When stripping formwork for a reinforced concrete beam, which part of the system must remain supported for the longest duration?
questions.n: The bottom forms (soffits) and the vertical supports (shores) must stay until the beam reaches sufficient strength to carry its own weight and any construction loads.

questions.q: In the Philippines, what is the nominal diameter of a #5 reinforcing steel bar?
questions.n: A #5 bar has a nominal diameter of approximately 16 mm.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of providing a 'camber' in the formwork of a long-span reinforced concrete beam?
o: To allow for better drainage on the floor above
To compensate for the expected downward deflection
To reduce the amount of concrete needed
To increase the compressive strength of the beam
questions.n: By curving the beam slightly upward during casting, it will appear level once it deflects under its own weight and permanent loads.

questions.q: Which admixture is used to reduce the amount of water needed for a specific workability, thereby increasing the concrete's strength?
questions.n: Also known as high-range water reducers, these allow for a very fluid mix without adding excess water.

questions.q: In a wood-framed wall, what is the name of the horizontal member that supports the ends of the studs at the bottom?
questions.n: The sole plate (or bottom plate) serves as the base for the vertical studs in a wall frame.

questions.q: What is the maximum allowable spacing of vertical bars in a load-bearing CHB wall according to the National Structural Code of the Philippines (NSCP)?
questions.n: The standard code requirement for vertical reinforcement spacing in masonry is often capped at 600 mm (approx. every 3 cells).

questions.q: Which phenomenon occurs when fresh concrete is vibrated too much, causing the heavy aggregates to sink and the water/laitance to rise?
questions.n: Excessive vibration breaks the bond of the mix, leading to an uneven distribution of materials.

questions.q: What is the minimum thickness for a load-bearing concrete hollow block (CHB) used for exterior walls in the Philippines?
questions.n: Load-bearing exterior walls generally require at least a 150 mm thickness for structural stability and weather protection.

questions.n: The 'L' stands for Angle, and the equal dimensions (100x100) indicate equal legs with a 10mm thickness.

questions.q: What is the primary reason for using 'Web Stiffeners' in a steel plate girder?
o: To prevent the web from buckling under concentrated loads
To increase the bending capacity of the flanges
questions.n: Thin webs are susceptible to local buckling, and stiffeners provide the necessary lateral rigidity.

questions.q: According to the NSCP, foundations should never be placed on which of the following materials?
questions.n: Foundations must rest on natural, undisturbed soil or properly engineered and compacted fill to prevent unpredictable settlement.
